scope: Selected reset scientific material properties with mutable reference mode/count/allocation; active populated objects included. No universal material/scientific model claim.

api.begin_material_reference_count: Require owned record and selected simulation profile; save old logical count, zero current count before reader.
api.apply_material_reference_count: Store parsed count even on failure. Failure leaves mode/allocation. Positive success sets mode1, frees old allocation then allocates zeroed int32 storage. Nonpositive success uses native guarded old-reference mode clearing and retains storage.
api.write_material_reference: Write one existing logical/allocated slot; reject out-of-range ownership or extent.
api.reference_ids: Logical positive prefix; empty for nonpositive count. Invalid positive extent rejected.
api.retained_reference_ids: Full owned retained allocation, independent of current signed logical count.
api.has_reference_allocation: Whether owned positive calloc-equivalent storage remains.

mutation_rules: MSTMTR common prefix may create a material and refresh objects before reading its count; importer owns that ordering.

Nonpositive successful count: only mode1 AND retained allocation AND previous count>0 visits exactly previous count IDs, exact-lookup targets setmode0, then source mode0. Guard failure leaves mode unchanged.

Finalizer1d6250 visits insertion order and reads source current count on each loop test. Resolved target mode!=2 with count>0 loses allocation/count, then mode2; count<=0 retains allocation/count and becomes mode2. Self/cycle effects are immediate.
MSTMTR mutation and reference finalization do not eagerly refresh components.
Feature49 is any material mode1 in selected root85c=0 reset profile; default remaining scientific flags remain zero.
Dimension reset destroys materials/reference allocations through existing owned-root reset.

remap.mapping: Before append save insertion-order old IDs; old rank is count of old IDs strictly less. New rank is count of current IDs strictly less, provided exact ID exists. 29c7f0 returns 1-based insertion position or-1; caller uses existence only.
remap.sequence: For option1 append with active feature49, capture old arrays49/50 before root layout; update root components; refresh each type!=7 object's storage then immediately zero/remap its arrays49/50. Configuration option0 only preserving refresh.
remap.storage: Native a58/a60 map to element descriptors49/50. Capture/remap uses header element count884 and root width49; allocation extents are checked separately.
remap.equation: For old-map column c<oldwidth: if ID survives, new[row*newwidth+newrank(ID[c])] = old[row*oldwidth+oldrank(ID[c])]. New destination prefixes are zeroed first.
remap.temporary_copy: Implementation snapshots just49/50 required values. Broader native temporary object copies are deep and observationally source-preserving in the owned profile established by material-object integration evidence. No temporary native pointer identity is promised.
remap.inactive: Type7 objects skip copy/resize/remap and retain their existing storage.

boundaries: Allocation failure and native signed extent arithmetic overflow are not emulated; checked owned extents and standard allocation exceptions avoid undefined C++ behavior.
Malformed external logical counts exceeding retained allocations, rank/width inconsistencies, and arbitrary shared/borrowed native pointers are rejected or excluded.

Importer owns finite double-to-int32 truncation and explicit unsupported first matching failure. Native nonfinite/out-of-range CVTTSD2SI and uninitialized local values are not assigned invented meanings.
Selected root85c remains reset0; nondefault material scientific properties and feature families remain outside this model.
Producer VOLFC/VOLFS is recovered separately, not implemented by this change. Nonzero original-array remap validation remains the next increment.
